GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 69: MACULAR DEGENERATION (AMD) AND CENTRAL VISION LOSS Section: Ophthalmology, Retinal Pathology & Vision Care Definition and Clinical Overview: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a progressive degenerative disease of the retinal macula, the specialized central area responsible for sharp, detailed vision.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Drusen lipid deposits between the retinal pigment epithelium and Bruch’s membrane (Dry AMD) or choroidal neovascularization with fluid leakage (Wet AMD). Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Use bright task lighting, use high-contrast reading aids, and monitor your vision using an Amsler grid covering one eye at a time.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Take AREDS2 antioxidant formula vitamins (under ophthalmologist guidance), quit smoking, consume dark leafy greens, and receive intravitreal anti-VEGF injections for wet AMD. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek same-day ophthalmological evaluation for any sudden distortion of straight lines (straight lines appearing wavy) or sudden dark blind spot in central vision.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 70: MENINGITIS, NUCHAL RIGIDITY AND NEUROLOGICAL RED FLAGS Section: Infectious Diseases, Neurology & Emergency Medicine Definition and Clinical Overview: Meningitis is an acute, life-threatening inflammation of the protective meningeal membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, caused by bacterial or viral pathogens.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Bacterial (Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae) or viral dissemination enters the subarachnoid space, triggering severe cerebral edema and intracranial pressure. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): This is a critical medical emergency. Do NOT attempt home self-care. Transport to the nearest emergency department immediately.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Immediate diagnostic lumbar puncture and prompt administration of empiric broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and corticosteroids; close contacts may require chemoprophylaxis. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Call 911 immediately for high fever, severe headache, stiff neck (inability to touch chin to chest), confusion, vomiting, and a non-blanching purple petechial rash.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 71: METABOLIC SYNDROME AND CARDIOMETABOLIC RISK Section: Endocrinology, Preventative Cardiology & Metabolism Definition and Clinical Overview: Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least 3 of 5 cardiometabolic risk factors: abdominal obesity, elevated triglycerides, low HDL, hypertension, and elevated fasting glucose.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Underlying insulin resistance, visceral adiposity, systemic pro-inflammatory adipokines, and physical inactivity. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Replace refined sugars and sodas with pure water, take a 20-minute brisk walk after meals, and prepare meals centered on high-fiber whole foods.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Target 5-10% gradual weight loss through regular physical activity (both aerobic and resistance training), adopt a Mediterranean diet, and control blood pressure and lipids. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical evaluation for persistent excessive thirst, frequent urination, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 72: MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AND DEMYELINATING CENTRAL PATHOLOGY Section: Neurology, Neuroimmunology & Demyelinating Disease Definition and Clinical Overview: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, characterized by episodic neurological attacks separated in time and space.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Autoreactive T-cells cross the blood-brain barrier and attack myelin sheaths and oligodendrocytes, slowing saltatory axonal nerve conduction. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rest in a cool air- conditioned room (avoid heat which worsens MS symptoms - Uhthoff’s phenomenon), stay hydrated, and use assistive devices for balance stability.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Undergo MRI evaluation and initiate disease-modifying therapies (DMTs: interferons, monoclonal antibodies) early to reduce relapses and slow disability accumulation. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek urgent neurological care for sudden loss of vision in one eye with pain on movement (optic neuritis), sudden limb paralysis, or loss of bladder control.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 73: MYASTHENIA GRAVIS AND NEUROMUSCULAR JUNCTION FATIGUE Section: Neurology, Neuromuscular Medicine & Autoimmunity Definition and Clinical Overview: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder characterized by fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Autoantibodies against the acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or MuSK block and destroy postsynaptic receptors, preventing normal muscle endplate depolarization. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rest quietly in a cool room, pace activities throughout the day, eat smaller soft meals when muscle strength is highest, and avoid strenuous physical exertion.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Take prescribed acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (pyridostigmine) and immunosuppressants; evaluate for thymoma with chest CT imaging and consider thymectomy. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care immediately for difficulty swallowing, choking on saliva, or shortness of breath (myasthenic crisis requiring respiratory support).

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 74: NON-ALCOHOLIC STEATOHEPATITIS (NASH/MASH) AND FIBROSIS Section: Hepatology, Gastroenterology & Metabolic Medicine Definition and Clinical Overview: MASH is the progressive inflammatory subtype of steatotic liver disease characterized by hepatic steatosis, hepatocyte ballooning, and progressive liver fibrosis.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Lipotoxicity from saturated free fatty acids, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction activate hepatic stellate cells to lay down collagen scar tissue. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Avoid all alcoholic beverages, eliminate refined sugars and high-fructose syrups, and engage in daily aerobic exercise.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Target 7-10% body weight loss, adopt an anti-inflammatory Mediterranean diet, optimize diabetes control, and undergo non-invasive elastography (FibroScan) monitoring. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical evaluation for persistent abdominal swelling, easy bruising, jaundice, or severe unexplained fatigue.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 75: OSTEOARTHRITIS, CARTILAGE DEGRADATION AND JOINT CARE Section: Rheumatology, Orthopedics & Geriatric Medicine Definition and Clinical Overview: Osteoarthritis is the most prevalent degenerative joint disease, characterized by progressive loss of articular cartilage, subchondral bone remodeling, and osteophyte formation.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Biomechanical joint stress, previous joint trauma, aging, and low-grade synovial inflammation breakdown the extracellular proteoglycan cartilage matrix. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rest the joint after prolonged use, apply cold packs for acute swelling or warm wraps for morning stiffness, and use a cane in the opposite hand if hip/knee is affected.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Engage in low-impact physical exercise (swimming, stationary cycling, water aerobics) to strengthen stabilizing muscles, manage body weight, and take NSAIDs as directed. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek orthopedic consultation if pain persists at rest, severely limits walking, or if the joint becomes locked or hot and red.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 76: OSTEOPOROSIS, DEXA SCANS AND FRACTURE PREVENTION Section: Endocrinology, Bone Mineralization & Geriatrics Definition and Clinical Overview: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disease defined by low bone mineral density (T-score ? -2.5 on DEXA) and microarchitectural deterioration of bone tissue, increasing fracture risk.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Bone resorption by osteoclasts outpaces bone formation by osteoblasts, accelerated by postmenopausal estrogen decline, aging, and calcium/Vitamin D deficiency. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Maintain clear walking pathways at home (remove loose throw rugs, ensure bright nightlights), wear non- skid supportive footwear, and avoid bending at the waist.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Perform weight-bearing and resistance exercises, ensure adequate dietary calcium (1200 mg/day) and Vitamin D (800-1000 IU/day), and take prescribed bisphosphonates. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency medical evaluation for sudden severe back pain following a minor fall (possible vertebral compression fracture) or inability to bear weight on the hip.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 77: OTITIS MEDIA, OTITIS EXTERNA AND EAR PAIN Section: Otolaryngology, Pediatric Medicine & Audiology Definition and Clinical Overview: Otitis media is acute inflammation and fluid accumulation in the middle ear space behind the tympanic membrane; otitis externa is infection of the external ear canal.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Eustachian tube dysfunction following an upper respiratory infection allows bacterial colonization (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae) in the middle ear. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Apply a warm moist compress over the affected ear, keep the head elevated, use over-the-counter pain relievers (acetaminophen or ibuprofen), and keep water out of the ear.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a healthcare provider for otoscopic examination; acute bacterial otitis media may require oral amoxicillin, while otitis externa requires antibiotic ear drops. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek urgent care for swelling or redness behind the ear over the mastoid bone (mastoiditis), high fever, severe dizziness, or fluid/blood draining from the ear.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 78: PANCREATITIS (ACUTE AND CHRONIC) & DIGESTIVE ENZYMES Section: Gastroenterology, Pancreatobiliary Medicine & Critical Care Definition and Clinical Overview: Acute pancreatitis is sudden inflammatory autodigestion of the pancreas caused by premature activation of pancreatic zymogens (trypsinogen) within acinar cells.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Gallstones obstructing the ampulla of Vater (biliary pancreatitis) and alcohol toxicity are responsible for over 70% of cases, followed by hypertriglyceridemia. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Do NOT eat or drink anything (bowel rest is essential), sit and lean forward to relieve back pain, and seek emergency hospital evaluation immediately.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Hospitalization for aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation, analgesia, and monitoring of serum lipase and amylase; gallstone cases require cholecystectomy. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Call 911 immediately for severe, sudden epigastric pain boring through to the back, accompanied by persistent vomiting, fever, rapid pulse, and dizziness.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 79: PARKINSON’S DISEASE, MOTOR SYMPTOMS AND NEUROPROTECTION Section: Neurology, Movement Disorders & Neurodegenerative Care Definition and Clinical Overview: Parkinson’s disease is a progressive neurodegenerative movement disorder characterized by resting tremor, bradykinesia (slowness), muscular rigidity, and postural instability.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, accompanied by intracellular alpha-synuclein protein inclusions (Lewy bodies). Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Take movement breaks, practice deliberate large-amplitude stepping (visualize stepping over lines), use supportive armchairs, and pace daily activities.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a movement disorder neurologist for individualized pharmacotherapy (levodopa/carbidopa, dopamine agonists), targeted physical therapy, and speech therapy. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care for sudden inability to swallow saliva, choking, sudden worsening confusion, or severe falls resulting in head injury.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 80: PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE (PID) AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH Section: Gynecology, Infectious Diseases & Reproductive Health Definition and Clinical Overview: Pelvic inflammatory disease is an ascending polymicrobial infection of the upper female genital tract (uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries), potentially causing infertility.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Ascending infection from sexually transmitted pathogens (Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae) or vaginal microflora past the endocervical barrier. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rest in bed, drink fluids, avoid sexual intercourse until treatment is completed, and seek prompt clinical gynecology evaluation.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Complete full-spectrum empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic regimens (ceftriaxone, doxycycline, metronidazole), and ensure all sexual partners are tested and treated. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency medical care for high fever, severe bilateral lower abdominal pain, vomiting, or signs of pelvic abscess.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 81: PERIPHERAL ARTERY DISEASE AND INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION Section: Vascular Surgery, Cardiology & Angiology Definition and Clinical Overview: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is atherosclerotic narrowing of peripheral systemic arteries, classical in the lower extremities causing exertional claudication.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Atherosclerotic plaque accumulation in femoral, popliteal, or iliac arteries leads to exercise-induced muscle ischemia that resolves within 10 minutes of rest. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Stop walking and rest in a seated position until calf cramping resolves, keep the feet warm with socks (avoid hot water bottles which cause burns), and protect feet.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Undergo ankle-brachial index (ABI) testing, participate in supervised treadmill walking exercise programs, stop smoking completely, and take prescribed antiplatelet therapy. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek urgent care for pain in the foot or toes at rest (critical limb ischemia), cold pale foot with absent pulses, or non-healing ulcers/black discoloration.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 82: PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY AND DIABETIC FOOT CARE Section: Neurology, Endocrinology & Podiatric Medicine Definition and Clinical Overview: Peripheral neuropathy is damage to peripheral nerves causing sensory loss, numbness, burning tingling (’pins and needles’), and weakness, common in diabetes.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Chronic hyperglycemia, microvascular endoneurial ischemia, advanced glycation end-products (AGEs), and sorbitol accumulation damage peripheral nerve fibers. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Inspect both feet daily using a mirror for any cuts, blisters, or redness; wash feet in lukewarm water, dry thoroughly between toes, and wear seamless white socks.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Maintain tight glycemic control, wear well-cushioned protective shoes, never walk barefoot, and take prescribed neuromodulating medications (duloxetine, gabapentin). Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek immediate medical attention for any open sore or ulcer on the foot, spreading redness, fever, or black discoloration.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 83: PHARYNGITIS, STREP THROAT AND TONSILLAR HEALTH Section: Otolaryngology, Infectious Diseases & Pediatric Care Definition and Clinical Overview: Pharyngitis is acute mucosal inflammation of the throat and tonsils, caused by respiratory viruses or Group A Streptococcus bacteria (strep throat).

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Bacterial colonization (Streptococcus pyogenes) causes acute follicular exudates, tonsillar swelling, palatal petechiae, and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Gargle with warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt in 8 oz water) every 3 hours, drink warm honey-lemon water or cool liquids, and take acetaminophen for throat pain.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Visit a clinic for a rapid strep antigen throat swab; confirmed strep throat requires a 10-day course of oral penicillin/amoxicillin to prevent acute rheumatic fever. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency medical evaluation for difficulty swallowing saliva (drooling), inability to open the mouth (trismus), muffled ’hot-potato’ voice, or labored breathing.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 84: PLANTAR FASCIITIS AND CALCANEAL HEEL PAIN Section: Podiatry, Orthopedic Medicine & Foot Biomechanics Definition and Clinical Overview: Plantar fasciitis is degenerative irritation and micro-tears of the thick plantar aponeurosis band connecting the calcaneus to the proximal phalanges.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Repetitive impact loading, sudden increase in running distance, prolonged standing on hard surfaces, flat feet (pes planus), tight Achilles tendons, and poor footwear. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Avoid walking barefoot, roll the arch of the foot over a frozen water bottle for 10 minutes, and perform gentle calf and plantar fascia stretches before stepping out of bed.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Wear supportive shoes with firm arch support and cushioned heels, use custom or over-the-counter orthotic inserts, and perform eccentric calf-strengthening exercises. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical evaluation if heel pain is accompanied by numbness/tingling in the toes, fever, or inability to bear any weight on the foot.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 85: PNEUMONIA (COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED) AND PULMONARY CONSOLIDATION Section: Pulmonology, Infectious Diseases & Critical Care Definition and Clinical Overview: Pneumonia is an acute infection of the pulmonary parenchyma (alveoli and bronchioles) resulting in inflammatory exudative consolidation and impaired gas exchange.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Inhalation or aspiration of pathogens (Streptococcus pneumoniae, atypical Mycoplasma, viruses) into terminal bronchioles, triggering alveolar neutrophilic exudation. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rest in bed, drink plenty of warm fluids to loosen secretions, use a cool-mist humidifier, and monitor blood oxygen levels with a pulse oximeter if available.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a healthcare provider for chest X-ray and targeted antibiotic or antiviral therapy; complete the full prescription and receive the pneumococcal vaccine. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care immediately for oxygen saturation below 92%, severe shortness of breath, confusion, coughing up blood, or blue tint to lips.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 86: PSORIASIS, PLAQUE DERMATITIS AND AUTOIMMUNE SKIN CARE Section: Dermatology, Autoimmune Pathology & Rheumatology Definition and Clinical Overview: Psoriasis is a chronic systemic immune-mediated dermatosis characterized by erythematous, well-demarcated plaques covered with coarse silvery scales.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Hyperactive dendritic cell and T-cell signaling (IL-17 / IL-23 axis) stimulates excessive keratinocyte proliferation, reducing epidermal turnover time from 28 to 4 days. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Apply a thick emollient or petroleum jelly immediately after bathing, avoid picking or scratching scales (which triggers Koebner phenomenon), and take a lukewarm bath.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a dermatologist for topical vitamin D analogues, topical corticosteroids, phototherapy, or targeted systemic biologic therapies (IL-17, IL-23 inhibitors). Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek urgent medical evaluation for widespread generalized fiery red skin with chills (erythrodermic psoriasis) or severe joint swelling (psoriatic arthritis).

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 87: PULMONARY FIBROSIS AND RESTRICTIVE LUNG DISEASE Section: Pulmonary Medicine & Interstitial Lung Disease Definition and Clinical Overview: Pulmonary fibrosis involves progressive, irreversible scarring and stiffening of the alveolar interstitium, impairing pulmonary compliance and oxygen diffusion.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Idiopathic causes, environmental dust/mineral exposures (silica, asbestos), autoimmune diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, scleroderma), or radiation therapy. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Avoid all tobacco smoke and airborne dust, use home supplemental oxygen as prescribed, pace daily tasks to prevent breathlessness, and stay up to date on vaccines.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a pulmonologist for high-resolution chest CT and pulmonary function tests; take antifibrotic medications (pirfenidone, nintedanib), and attend pulmonary rehab. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care for acute, rapidly worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or low blood oxygen saturation.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 88: RAYNAUD’S PHENOMENON AND DIGITAL VASOSPASM Section: Rheumatology, Vascular Medicine & Microcirculation Definition and Clinical Overview: Raynaud’s phenomenon is an episodic, exaggerated vasospastic disorder of digital arteries and arterioles in response to cold temperatures or emotional stress.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Hyperactivity of the sympathetic nervous system and local vascular endothelial dysfunction lead to triphasic color changes: white (pallor), blue (cyanosis), red (rubor). Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rewarm the hands and feet gently in warm (not hot) water, place hands under armpits, move to a warm room, and wiggle the fingers and toes.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Wear warm gloves or mittens, avoid handling cold items directly, avoid tobacco and caffeine which constrict blood vessels, and discuss calcium channel blockers with a doctor. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical evaluation for painful non-healing sores or ulcers on the fingertips, or sudden blackened skin indicating digital gangrene.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 89: RESTLESS LEGS SYNDROME AND SLEEP DISRUPTION Section: Neurology, Sleep Medicine & Dopaminergic Function Definition and Clinical Overview: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a neurological sensorimotor disorder characterized by an irresistible urge to move the legs, typically during evening rest.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Central brain iron deficiency in the substantia nigra, dopaminergic neurotransmission dysfunction, and genetic variations in sleep architecture genes. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Get up and walk, gently stretch the calf and hamstring muscles, massage the legs, or take a warm bath before bedtime.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Check serum ferritin levels (supplement iron if ferritin <75 ng/mL), avoid caffeine, alcohol, and antihistamines in the evening, and take prescribed alpha-2-delta ligands. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical review for daytime sleepiness that impairs driving or work safety, or if involuntary daytime limb movements occur.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 90: RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS, SYNOVITIS AND AUTOIMMUNE JOINT CARE Section: Rheumatology, Autoimmunity & Synovial Pathology Definition and Clinical Overview: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease primarily attacking synovial joint linings in a symmetric polyarticular pattern.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Loss of self-tolerance to citrullinated peptides leads to RF and anti-CCP autoantibodies, synovial proliferation (pannus formation), and joint bone erosion. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Apply warm moist compresses for morning joint stiffness, use cold packs for acute inflamed joint flares, and rest the affected joints.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a rheumatologist early for disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs: methotrexate) and biologic agents to prevent permanent joint deformities. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical evaluation for high fever with a single hot swollen joint (to rule out septic arthritis) or acute neck pain with neurological numbness.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 91: ROSACEA, FACIAL FLUSHING AND CUTANEOUS CAPILLARIES Section: Dermatology, Vascular Dermatology & Facial Skin Care Definition and Clinical Overview: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis affecting the central face, featuring recurrent flushing, persistent erythema, telangiectasias, and inflammatory papules.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Cutaneous neurovascular dysregulation, innate immune antimicrobial peptide hyperreactivity (cathelicidins), and Demodex folliculorum mite proliferation. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Apply a cool water compress to the face, move into an air-conditioned room, sip ice water, and avoid known dietary triggers (spicy food, hot beverages, alcohol).

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Use mineral sunscreen daily (zinc oxide), wash face with gentle fragrance-free cleansers, avoid harsh scrubs, and use prescribed topical ivermectin or metronidazole. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek ophthalmological care for gritty eye sensation, eyelid inflammation, or redness (ocular rosacea which can damage the cornea).

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 92: SCABIES, PEDICULOSIS AND PARASITIC DERMATOSES Section: Dermatology, Parasitology & Public Health Definition and Clinical Overview: Scabies is an intensely pruritic, contagious parasitic skin infestation caused by the microscopic itch mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Female mites burrow into the epidermal stratum corneum, depositing eggs and feces, which trigger a severe delayed-type allergic hypersensitivity reaction. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Apply cool compresses or calamine lotion to soothe itching, avoid scratching to prevent bacterial impetigo, and wash all bedding in very hot water.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a doctor for topical permethrin 5% cream applied from neck to toes overnight, wash all clothing and linens in hot water, and treat all household contacts simultaneously. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical attention for spreading skin redness, warmth, pus, or fever indicating secondary bacterial infection.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 93: SCIATICA, HERNIATED LUMBAR DISC & RADICULOPATHY Section: Orthopedic Spine Surgery, Neurology & Pain Medicine Definition and Clinical Overview: Sciatica refers to radiating pain along the course of the sciatic nerve (from lower back through buttock and down the posterior leg), most commonly from disc herniation.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Posterolateral herniation of the L4-L5 or L5-S1 nucleus pulposus mechanically compresses the exiting nerve root, producing chemical radiculitis and sharp radiating pain. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Avoid sitting for prolonged periods, lie on a firm surface on your back with pillows beneath knees, apply ice packs to the lower back, and take short gentle walks.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Perform gentle nerve- flossing exercises, avoid forward bending while lifting, pursue physical therapy, and consider epidural steroid injection if conservative care fails. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care immediately for loss of bowel or bladder control, numbness in the saddle/groin area, or progressive muscle weakness in the leg/foot.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 94: SCOLIOSIS, SPINAL ALIGNMENT AND POSTURAL SCREENING Section: Orthopedic Spine Surgery & Physical Rehabilitation Definition and Clinical Overview: Scoliosis is a three-dimensional structural deformity of the spine characterized by a lateral curvature in the coronal plane of at least 10 degrees (Cobb angle).

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (80% of cases) has multifactorial genetic and asymmetric growth plate origins; adult degenerative scoliosis stems from asymmetric disc wear. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Practice core stabilization exercises, maintain upright sitting posture, and engage in low- impact swimming to support paraspinal muscular balance.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Undergo regular orthopedic scoliosis monitoring; curves 25-40 degrees in growing adolescents benefit from corrective bracing; curves >45-50 degrees may warrant surgery. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical evaluation for progressive shortness of breath, severe unremitting back pain, or progressive leg numbness/weakness.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 95: SINUSITIS (ACUTE AND CHRONIC RHINOSINUSITIS) Section: Otolaryngology, Rhinology & Upper Airway Health Definition and Clinical Overview: Sinusitis is inflammation of the mucosal lining of the paranasal sinuses and nasal cavity, characterized by nasal congestion, facial pressure, and purulent discharge.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Obstruction of the sinus ostia following a viral cold, mucosal edema, and impaired ciliary clearance allow mucus stagnation and secondary bacterial infection. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Perform nasal saline irrigations using a neti pot with sterile water, inhale warm steam from a bowl or shower, apply warm face compresses, and stay hydrated.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Use intranasal corticosteroid sprays; viral sinusitis resolves in 7-10 days; bacterial sinusitis (symptoms >10 days or ’double-sickening’) requires amoxicillin-clavulanate. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care for swelling or redness around the eye, vision changes, severe frontal headache with fever, or stiff neck.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 96: SLEEP APNEA (OBSTRUCTIVE) AND NOCTURNAL HYPOXEMIA Section: Sleep Medicine, Pulmonology & Upper Airway Physiology Definition and Clinical Overview: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is characterized by repetitive episodes of complete (apnea) or partial (hypopnea) upper airway collapse during sleep.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Pharyngeal muscle relaxation during REM and deep sleep allows the tongue and soft palate to obstruct the airway, causing episodic hypoxemia and cortical arousals. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Sleep on your side rather than your back (positional therapy), avoid alcohol and sedatives before bed, and elevate the head of the bed.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Undergo a polysomnography sleep study; first-line therapy is nocturnal Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP), weight management, or oral mandibular advancement splints. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek medical evaluation for severe daytime sleepiness, falling asleep while driving, witnessed nocturnal choking/gasping, or uncontrolled morning hypertension.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 97: SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS (SLE) AND AUTOIMMUNITY Section: Rheumatology, Autoimmune Connective Tissue Disease Definition and Clinical Overview: Systemic lupus erythematosus is a multisystem autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by antibodies against nuclear antigens (ANA) and immune-complex deposition.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Defective clearance of apoptotic debris exposes nuclear antigens to autoantibodies, forming immune complexes that deposit in kidneys, skin, joints, and serosa. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Avoid direct sunlight and UV exposure (wear sun-protective clothing and SPF 50+ sunscreen), get plenty of restorative rest, and manage emotional stress.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a rheumatologist for regular disease monitoring; first-line therapy is hydroxychloroquine, along with targeted immunosuppressants and kidney function surveillance. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care for chest pain worse with breathing (pericarditis/pleuritis), shortness of breath, new confusion, or rapidly swelling legs with foamy urine.

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 98: TENDONITIS (ACHILLES, PATELLAR AND BICIPITAL) Section: Sports Medicine, Physical Therapy & Tendinopathy Definition and Clinical Overview: Tendonitis is acute inflammation and micro- injury of a tendon, the fibrous connective tissue structure that anchors muscle to bone.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Repetitive mechanical overload, abrupt increases in training volume, improper biomechanics, and inadequate recovery create micro-tears in collagen fibers. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rest from aggravating repetitive movements, apply ice packs wrapped in a towel for 15 minutes 3 times daily, and use a supportive brace or wrap.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Perform gentle eccentric strengthening exercises (such as heel drops for Achilles), avoid aggressive stretching of the inflamed tendon, and pursue physical therapy. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek urgent orthopedic evaluation for a sudden loud ’pop’ or snap accompanied by immediate severe pain and inability to move the limb (tendon rupture).

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 99: TONSILLITIS, PERITONSILLAR ABSCESS AND PHARYNGEAL HEALTH Section: Otolaryngology, Infectious Diseases & Airway Safety Definition and Clinical Overview: Tonsillitis is acute infection and inflammatory swelling of the palatine tonsils, accompanied by sore throat, fever, and painful swallowing (odynophagia).

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Respiratory viruses or Group A Streptococcus bacteria infect tonsillar crypts, triggering tonsillar erythema, exudates, and jugulodigastric lymphadenopathy. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Gargle with warm salt water every 2-3 hours, drink cool soothing liquids or fruit smoothies, use throat lozenges, and take acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a healthcare provider for throat swab testing; confirmed strep requires antibiotics; recurrent severe episodes may warrant tonsillectomy consultation. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency care immediately for difficulty breathing, drooling, inability to swallow liquids, or severe unilateral throat swelling with a deviated uvula (peritonsillar abscess).

GALE ENCYCLOPEDIA OF MEDICINE PAGE 100: ULCERATIVE COLITIS AND MUCOSAL COLONIC REMISSION Section: Gastroenterology, Colorectal Surgery & IBD Care Definition and Clinical Overview: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease causing continuous, superficial mucosal inflammation and ulcerations extending proximally from the rectum.

What Is the Reason (Underlying Etiology & Mechanisms): Dysregulated colonic mucosal immune response against commensal gut microbiota in genetically predisposed individuals, causing crypt abscesses and friability. Immediate Action Plan (What to Do Right Now for Relief): Rest, drink oral rehydration fluids with electrolytes, eat small bland meals (bananas, white rice), and avoid spicy, high-fat, or high-fiber foods during acute flares.

Proper Plan: How to Cure & Prevent (Long-Term Management): Consult a gastroenterologist for colonoscopy staging and long-term maintenance therapy (oral 5-ASAs like mesalamine, biologics, or JAK inhibitors), with annual colon cancer screening. Red-Flag Warning Signs (When to Seek Emergency Care): Seek emergency medical evaluation for heavy rectal bleeding, high fever, severe abdominal pain, or rapid abdominal distension with tachycardia (toxic megacolon).
